name: Life360 Design System
summary: Recreate Life360's map-first family-safety UI in SwiftUI, built around per-member identity colors, a violet brand spine, and rationed safety-red.
description: A production-ready prompt for rebuilding Life360's map-first iOS experience in SwiftUI, covering the fixed per-member identity color system, the Circle selector and draggable member sheet, geofence Places, and the press-and-hold SOS flow.

whatYouGet: A full SwiftUI color, type and component token set matching Life360's violet-and-member-color system, ready to drop into a project
Working code for the signature Member Pin, Circle Selector pill, member sheet row and press-and-hold SOS button, including motion and haptics
House rules that keep member identity colors, safety-red rationing and map styling consistent as new screens are added
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in cloning best-in-class consumer app design systems into pixel-accurate, production-ready SwiftUI code. You have deep fluency in family-safety and location-sharing apps and understand why map-first products live or die on the legibility of their in-context color coding.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from a real map-first family-safety app's design system (use these as ground truth, do not invent alternates):

Color roles:
- Brand violet: #582C83 (deep, spine only) and #7E57C2 (working UI tint: buttons, active tab, Circle selector accent), #8B5CF6 (emphasis/focus), #4A2470 (pressed)
- Night canvas: #161325; Surface 1 (cards/pill) #1F1B33; Surface 2 (pressed/chips) #2A2542; Sheet/tab bar #211D36; Divider #332E4D; Border #3D3759
- Map palette (dark-styled to keep pins salient): base #1A2138, roads #2C3654, parks #1B3A2E, water #16314A, labels #7E7A99
- Text: primary #ECEAF5 (dark) / #1C1830 (light), secondary #A6A0C2, tertiary #6F6990
- Per-member identity colors (assigned in join order, fixed forever per person): amber #F2A33C, teal #2DD4BF, pink #F472B6, blue #60A5FA, purple #7E57C2 (only if brand purple is otherwise reserved), coral #FB7185, lime #A3E635, sky #38BDF8
- Safety semantics (rationed hard): safe green #34C759, SOS/alert red #FF6B6B, warning amber #FFB020, neutral/info purple #7E57C2

Type ladder (single face, Plus Jakarta Sans, weights 400/600/700/800, fallback -apple-system/SF Pro/Segoe UI/Roboto):
- Display 32pt/800, Title 26pt/700, Section 22pt/700, Member Name 18pt/700, Body 16pt/400, Row Title 15pt/600, Place/Status 13pt/600, Meta 14pt/400, Caption 12pt/600 uppercase eyebrow, Pin Initial 16pt/700, Tab Label 10pt/600, Button 15pt/700, SOS Label 15pt/800 +0.5pt tracking

Spacing / radius / shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/28/32/40/48
- Radius scale: 8pt small chips, 12pt nested cards, 16pt fields/panels, 22pt sheets, 28pt tall pill buttons, 999pt full pills/chips, 50% circles for pins/avatars
- Elevation is real and soft (not flat): pins/tags shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.5) 0 4px 12px; floating chrome (Circle pill) rgba(0,0,0,0.45) 0 6px 20px + backdrop blur; bottom sheet rgba(0,0,0,0.5) 0 -8px 30px

Distinctive named UI patterns (reproduce faithfully):
1. Member Pin — a circular member photo/avatar in a 3pt solid white ring with an 8pt downward triangular pointer anchoring it to a map coordinate; grows to a 4pt ring + member-color glow when selected
2. Circle Selector pill — top-floating, translucent surface with backdrop blur, circle name + chevron, trailing bell icon with a red badge dot for unread alerts
3. Draggable bottom Member Sheet — multi-detent (peek/half/full), grabber handle, rows of name + place/status + battery indicator
4. Place Geofence — a translucent brand-tint circle on the map with a small emoji-tagged place pill, soft ripple pulse on member entry
5. Press-and-hold SOS button — radial fill progress over ~1.5s with an escalating haptic ramp; release-before-complete cancels with a spring-back
6. Breadcrumb trail — a member's recent path line drawn in their own identity color, so it is attributable without a legend
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Every person gets ONE fixed identity color assigned at join time, reused everywhere they appear (map pin, avatar, trail, driving report, detail header) — never reassign or reuse a color across two active members.
2. The brand violet is the spine (Circle UI, Places, CTAs, active tab) and must NEVER double as a member identity color, even when the palette runs short.
3. Safety-state red and green are rationed: red only fires for a genuine safety event (SOS, crash, unexpected place departure, critical low battery) — never use it for ordinary UI emphasis or errors.
4. Style the map dark by default (deep base, muted/desaturated roads, parks and water) so the colorful member pins remain the single brightest thing on screen; never fall back to a bright day map style at night.
5. Every member row must always show a battery reading — this is a safety affordance, not a nice-to-have, and it must never be dropped even in a compact layout.
6. Chrome floats above the map with real, soft, dark shadows (not flat cards) because the map is a literal spatial plane the UI must visibly hover over; use backdrop blur on translucent floating pills so the map is faintly visible through them.
7. Member pins and breadcrumb trails animate along their actual path when location updates — never teleport a pin; add a brief scale-pulse on update so a change is noticeable without being alarming.
8. The SOS control must never be a single quick tap: implement it as press-and-hold with a visible progress fill and an escalating haptic, and always provide a non-gestural fallback entry point for accessibility.
9. Keep type weights in a warm, confident register (700 for names, 800 for display/SOS) using a rounded-humanist face — avoid thin or corporate-cold weights anywhere a worried user might be reading.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [name of the app you are building]
- Platform target: [iOS version, SwiftUI minimum deployment target]
- Core entity being tracked: [family members / delivery drivers / pets / assets — whatever populates the map]
- Number of concurrent tracked entities per group: [e.g. 4-8 family members]
- Safety or alert events you need to support: [e.g. SOS, geofence exit, low battery, custom]
- Existing brand accent color (if any), to reconcile against the violet spine: [hex or "none yet"]
- Map provider you're integrating: [MapKit / Google Maps SDK / other]
- Screens in scope for this pass: [e.g. map home, member sheet, Places, SOS flow, driving reports]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` token extension file matching the reference palette and type ladder above, adapted to the project's entity names.
2. Working SwiftUI view code for the Member Pin (or your entity's pin), the Circle/group selector pill, and the draggable bottom sheet with detents.
3. A per-entity identity-color assignment strategy (enum or lookup) that guarantees no two active entities in the same group ever share a color.
4. The press-and-hold SOS (or equivalent critical-alert) control with progress fill, haptic ramp, and an accessible non-gestural fallback.
5. A dark-styled map configuration snippet (MapKit `MKMapConfiguration` or equivalent) tuned to keep colorful pins salient.
6. A motion/haptics cheat sheet (durations, easing curves, spring parameters) for pin movement, sheet drag, geofence ripple and SOS hold.
7. A short accessibility checklist covering VoiceOver labels for pins/rows, Reduce Motion fallbacks, and color-blind-safe redundancy (name + color, not color alone).
</what_to_give_me>

name: Midjourney Design System
summary: Recreate Midjourney's true-black, no-accent gallery UI in SwiftUI, centered on the 2x2 grid hero, monospace prompts and the U/V chip grammar.
description: A production-ready prompt for rebuilding Midjourney's OLED-black, imagery-first iOS design system in SwiftUI, including the job feed, prompt bar, and the Discord-heritage U1-U4/V1-V4 chip grammar.

whatYouGet: A SwiftUI color and type token set for a true-black, no-brand-accent gallery app, distinguishing UI sans from prompt monospace
Working code for the job card, 2x2 image grid, prompt bar, and the U-chip/V-chip action grammar with shimmer-to-resolve motion
House rules that protect the deliberate absence of a brand accent color and the monospace-for-instructions convention as the app grows
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in cloning generative-media and creative-tool interfaces into precise, production-ready SwiftUI. You understand why an imagery-first product deliberately removes brand color from its own chrome so generated content can be the only saturated thing on screen.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from a real AI image-generation app's design system:

Color roles (dark-only, no light mode):
- True black canvas #000000 (OLED black, not a warm charcoal)
- Surface 1 #0E0E0E (cards/sheets), Surface 2 #1A1A1A (input fill/ghost buttons), Surface 3 #242424 (pressed/scrubber), Divider #2A2A2A
- Text: primary #FFFFFF, secondary #A1A1A1, tertiary #6E6E6E
- The only "primary" interactive color is white #FFFFFF (pressed #DADADA) — there is deliberately no brand accent
- Heritage/secondary accents: rate/link blue #2D7FF9, and a legacy Discord blurple #4D5BCE reserved strictly for account/Discord-connect, never a general CTA
- Semantic: success green #2ECC71, warning amber #F5A623, error red #E5484D

Type ladder (two voices — UI sans + Inter fallback -apple-system/SF Pro/Segoe UI/Roboto, and prompt/parameter monospace SF Mono, JetBrains Mono fallback):
- Screen Title 32pt/800, Nav Title 22pt/700, Section 19pt/700, Body 16pt/400, Action/Tab-Active 15pt/600, Card Title 15pt/600, Prompt Text (mono) 13pt/400, Parameter Chip (mono) 13pt/600, Job Chip U1/V1 (mono) 13pt/600 +0.2pt, Metadata 14pt/400, Caption 12pt/500, Tab Label 10pt/500

Spacing / radius / shadow:
- Base spacing unit 2pt (tight), scale 2/4/6/8/10/14/18/24/32/48; grid cell seam 6pt; job-card vertical gap 18pt; screen horizontal inset 14pt
- Radius scale: 6pt subtle inner cell rounding, 8pt job/parameter chips and ghost buttons, 12pt image-grid container/cards, 16pt sheets, 25pt prompt-bar pill, 999pt primary buttons, 50% circular send button
- Depth is radically flat: a 1pt #2A2A2A hairline border is the primary "floats above black" cue (drop shadows are nearly invisible on true black); only bottom sheets/menus get a faint shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.6) 0 8px 24px)

Distinctive named UI patterns (reproduce faithfully):
1. Job Card — monospace prompt line above a 2x2 image grid above a compact action row; the atomic unit of the feed, newest job animating in at the top
2. 2x2 image grid — the hero unit; container reshapes to the prompt's aspect-ratio parameter while the 2x2 cell structure itself never changes; 6pt black seam between cells
3. U1-U4 / V1-V4 chip grammar (Discord-bot heritage) — white "do-it-now" upscale chips vs. dark "explore-from" variation chips, plus a re-roll chip; the grammar's ordering must never be swapped
4. Prompt bar — a pinned full-height pill with a monospace-typed prompt and a circular white Imagine send button; on focus, a horizontally-scrolling parameter helper strip of --flag chips slides up
5. Progress blur to resolve — a rendering job shows a shimmering blurred placeholder with a percentage, then crossfades into four sharp images with a slight scale-up on completion
6. Monospace-for-instructions convention — any prompt text or --flag parameter is always rendered in monospace, never the UI sans, because it is treated as a literal instruction rather than prose
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never introduce a brand accent color anywhere in chrome — white is the only primary, and any temptation to add a tinted CTA or an active-tab pill must be resisted.
2. The canvas must be literal, pure #000000 — not a softened near-black — because the entire point is OLED true-black behind full-color generated imagery.
3. Render every prompt string and every --flag parameter in monospace, never in the UI sans face; this is the single signal that tells a user "this is an instruction, not prose."
4. Never tint, filter, or overlay generated imagery for theming purposes — the grid is the only source of color in the whole interface and must render verbatim.
5. Preserve the U/V chip grammar exactly as specified: upscale chips are the bright/white "act now" affordance, variation chips are dark/outlined "explore further" affordances — do not invent a third chip style or reorder them.
6. Use a 1pt hairline border, not a shadow, as the primary way a floating element signals it is above the canvas — shadows are nearly invisible on true black and should only reinforce, never carry, elevation.
7. Keep navigation motion silent — tab switches are an instant color swap with no slide transition, while content within a job card (shimmer, resolve, chip flash) is where all the motion budget goes.
8. Reshape the image-grid container to the prompt's aspect ratio (square, landscape, portrait) while keeping the 2x2 internal grid structure fixed — never change the count or arrangement of cells.
9. Keep screen insets tight (roughly 14pt) and cell seams minimal (roughly 6pt) so the maximum possible pixel area is devoted to the rendered imagery rather than to chrome padding.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [name of the app you are building]
- Platform target: [iOS version, SwiftUI minimum deployment target]
- Type of generated/created content per job: [images / video / audio / other, and how many results per job]
- Prompt syntax you support: [natural language only / flag-style parameters / structured fields]
- Actions available per result: [e.g. upscale, variation, re-roll, edit, download, favorite]
- Community or discovery surface needed: [masonry feed, none, curated]
- Existing brand identity constraints (if any) you must reconcile against "no accent color": [describe]
- Screens in scope for this pass: [e.g. feed, prompt composer, lightbox, profile]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` token extension distinguishing the UI-sans voice from the prompt/parameter monospace voice, matching the reference values above.
2. Working SwiftUI view code for the Job Card (prompt line + 2x2 grid + action row), the prompt bar with an inline parameter helper strip, and the U/V chip cluster.
3. The shimmer-placeholder-to-resolve animation sequence (percentage counter, crossfade, scale) as reusable SwiftUI modifiers.
4. A lightbox/full-screen viewer with swipeable quadrants and a bottom action bar, matching the flat, border-not-shadow elevation model.
5. A short rationale note explaining, in your own words, why this product removed a brand accent color and how that decision should guide any new screen you design for it.
6. An accessibility pass covering VoiceOver labeling for grid cells and chips, Reduce Motion substitutes for the shimmer/resolve/lightbox spring, and Reduce Transparency handling for the blurred tab bar.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Perplexity Design System
summary: Recreate Perplexity's near-black, teal-accented answer-engine UI in SwiftUI, with inline citation chips, source cards and a two-face type system.
description: A production-ready prompt for rebuilding Perplexity's research-notebook iOS design system in SwiftUI, covering the signature cyan-teal accent, inline numbered citations, the horizontal source-card row, and the Pro Search reasoning trace.

whatYouGet: A SwiftUI color and type token set for a near-black, single-teal-accent answer-engine, split between a chrome typeface and a body typeface
Working code for the inline citation chip, the horizontal source-card row, the search input with its focus glow, and the collapsible Pro Search steps card
House rules that protect the single-accent discipline, the inline-citation pattern and the search-not-chat framing as new screens are added
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in cloning research and answer-engine interfaces into precise, production-ready SwiftUI. You understand the structural difference between a chat surface and a search surface, and why a citation-first product treats its accent color as a scarce, single-purpose signal.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from a real AI answer-engine app's design system:

Color roles (dark-first, light mode supported):
- Canvas #0A0A0A (near-black); Surface 1 #171717 (inputs/source cards), Surface 2 #1F1F1F (chips/pressed), Surface 3 #2A2A2A (sheets); Divider #2A2A2A
- Text: primary #FAFAFA (deliberately off-white, never pure #FFFFFF), secondary #A1A1A1, tertiary #6E6E6E, muted #4A4A4A
- The single signature accent is a cool cyan-teal: base #20B8CD, bright/hover #3DD6EC, deep/pressed #1591A3, soft background wash #0F3A42
- Semantic: success #22C55E, warning #F59E0B, error #EF4444, and a reserved premium gold #E0B341 used sparingly for "Pro" badges only
- Light mode darkens the teal to #1591A3 for contrast and flips canvas to #FFFFFF, but keeps every accent role otherwise identical

Type ladder (two-face system: FK Grotesk for chrome/brand voice, Inter for answer body, fallback -apple-system/SF Pro Display/Helvetica Neue):
- Display 30pt/700, Question Title 22pt/600, Section Header 18pt/600, Subsection 16pt/600, Answer Body (Inter) 16pt/400 at 1.5 line-height, Source Card Title 13pt/500, Source Card Domain 11pt/400, Citation Chip number (mono variant) 11pt/500, Button 15pt/600, Tab Label 10pt/500, Code Block (JetBrains Mono) 14pt/400

Spacing / radius / shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/48/56/64; standard horizontal margin 16pt on lists, 24pt on the search input; 32pt gap between an answer block and related questions
- Radius scale: 4pt citation chips/badges, 8pt code blocks and secondary pills, 10pt primary pills, 12pt cards (source cards, steps card), 24pt the search input (the only place this radius is used), 28pt the Pro Search toggle capsule, 50% send-button circle
- Elevation stays subtle (0.4-0.7 opacity shadows, 1-24pt blur) except for one deliberate exception: a soft cyan focus glow (rgba(32,184,205,0.25) 0 0 0 4px) around the focused search input — the single "glow" moment in the whole app

Distinctive named UI patterns (reproduce faithfully):
1. Inline citation chip — small numbered pills like [1] [2] [3] set directly within the answer prose (not only at the end), tappable to scroll to the matching source; teal border and text on focus
2. Source card row — a horizontal scroll of fixed 200x80pt cards (favicon + domain + truncated title + numeric badge) sitting above every answer, before any prose renders
3. "Searching the web..." indicator — three teal dots pulsing in staggered sequence shown immediately on submit, before source cards arrive
4. Streaming response cursor — a small blinking teal caret at the trailing edge of streaming text
5. Pro Search Steps card — a collapsible teal-tinted card above the answer that reveals a multi-step reasoning trace, each step showing a completion checkmark
6. The triple-circle/asterisk brand mark rendered exclusively in the teal accent, never any other color, at every size from avatar to splash
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Treat the teal accent as a single, scarce signal reserved for the send button, focus rings, citation chip outlines, the brand mark and active states — never let it leak into body text or decorative fills.
2. Never use pure white for primary text on the dark canvas; the correct value is an off-white that reads softer and reduces glare.
3. Keep the two-face typography split intact: the chrome/brand voice uses the geometric grotesque, the answer prose uses the body sans — never let answer text render in the chrome face or vice versa.
4. Citation chips live inline within the running prose, not bundled only at the end of the answer — this inline placement is the core differentiator from a plain footnote list.
5. Never render an answer without its source-card row above it; the source row appearing before the prose is the brand's proof-of-work moment and must not be optional.
6. Do not adopt a chat-bubble-with-tails pattern for the question or the answer — this is a search-and-cite surface, not a conversational thread, and should never visually imply back-and-forth messaging.
7. Avoid a warm accent (orange, red) anywhere in the interactive palette — the cool teal is chosen specifically to read as informational and clinical, and a warm color would contradict that register.
8. Reserve the teal focus glow specifically for the search input's focused state; do not scatter glow effects elsewhere, since its rarity is what makes it legible as "the one active field."
9. Use dark text on any teal-filled surface (buttons, badges) rather than white, to satisfy contrast against the mid-brightness accent color.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [name of the app you are building]
- Platform target: [iOS version, SwiftUI minimum deployment target]
- Query/answer flow: [single-turn search, multi-turn thread, or both]
- Source/citation model: [web sources, internal documents, both, none]
- Reasoning-trace feature needed: [yes/no — expandable multi-step trace like Pro Search]
- Existing brand accent (if any) to reconcile against the single-teal rule: [hex or "none yet"]
- Organizational features needed: [saved collections/threads, discovery feed, none]
- Screens in scope for this pass: [e.g. home search, answer view, sidebar/history, discover feed]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` token extension matching the reference palette and two-face type ladder above, with light-mode teal adjustment included.
2. Working SwiftUI view code for the search input (with focus glow), the citation chip, and the horizontal source-card row with its trailing "show all sources" affordance.
3. A collapsible reasoning-trace / Pro-Steps card component with per-step completion state and an accordion expand animation.
4. The "searching..." loading-dot sequence and the streaming-cursor blink as reusable SwiftUI view modifiers.
5. A short design rationale explaining, in your own words, why this product frames itself as search rather than chat and how that should influence any new screen added later.
6. An accessibility pass covering VoiceOver labeling for citation chips and source cards, Dynamic Type behavior (which elements scale vs. stay fixed), and contrast validation for teal-on-dark and dark-on-teal combinations.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Postman Design System
summary: Recreate Postman's neutral-grey developer-console UI in SwiftUI, built on the HTTP-method color system, mono-for-data typography and rationed brand orange.
description: A production-ready prompt for rebuilding Postman's API-console iOS design system in SwiftUI, covering the method-colored URL bar, the sans/mono content split, status-code chips, and the syntax-highlighted JSON viewer.

whatYouGet: A SwiftUI color and type token set encoding the HTTP-method color system, status-code classes and the sans-for-chrome/mono-for-data split
Working code for the method-colored URL/request bar, key-value editor rows, status chips and a syntax-highlighted JSON response block
House rules that keep brand orange rationed to actions only and method colors consistent everywhere a request or response appears
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in cloning developer-tool interfaces into precise, production-ready SwiftUI. You understand why an API console needs its own semantic color grammar distinct from its brand color, and why a request/response instrument reads fastest when data and chrome use two different typefaces.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from a real API-client app's design system:

Color roles (dark default, light supported):
- Dark canvas #1A1A1A (neutral grey, not pure black, not charcoal-blue); Surface 1 #212121 (cards/URL bar), Surface 2 #2A2A2A (pressed rows), Surface 3 #333333 (inline chips), Code Surface #161616 (darker than canvas, for response JSON); Divider #3A3A3A, Border #444444
- Text: primary #E8E8E8, secondary #A6A6A6, tertiary #6E6E6E
- The single brand accent is an orange: #FF6C37 base, #E55A2B pressed, a 12%-opacity wash #3D2417 for disabled/selected contexts — reserved strictly for actions (send, primary buttons, active tab, links), never decorative
- HTTP-method colors (fixed hue per method everywhere it appears, softened on dark vs. saturated on light): GET green #6BDD9A, POST yellow #FFE47A, PUT blue #74AEF6, PATCH purple #C0A8E1, DELETE red #F79090, OPTIONS/HEAD grey #A6A6A6
- Status-code classes: 2xx success green #6BDD9A, 3xx redirect blue #74AEF6, 4xx client error yellow #FFE47A, 5xx server error red #F79090
- JSON syntax colors: key blue #74AEF6, string green #6BDD9A, number/boolean/null purple #C0A8E1, punctuation dim grey #6E6E6E

Type ladder (sans for chrome, Inter fallback -apple-system/SF Pro/Segoe UI/Roboto; mono for all machine data, JetBrains Mono fallback SF Mono/Menlo/Consolas):
- Display 32pt/800, Title 26pt/700, Section 22pt/700, Subsection 18pt/600, Body 16pt/400, Label 15pt/500, Method Pill (mono) 13pt/700 +0.3pt tracking, URL/JSON (mono) 13pt/400-500, JSON Body (mono) 12pt/400 at 1.6 line-height, Status Code (mono) 12pt/700, Meta 14pt/400, Tab Label 10pt/500

Spacing / radius / shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt, scale 4/6/8/10/12/14/16/20/24/28/32; URL-bar internal segment padding 12pt; key-value row gap 8pt; screen horizontal inset 14-18pt
- Radius scale: 4pt inline code chips, 6pt method chips and key-value cells, 8pt buttons/inputs/response block, 10pt the URL/request bar, 16pt sheets/modals, 999pt pill status chips, 50% circular avatars
- Elevation is restrained: a 1pt border plus a slightly lighter surface does most separation work; genuinely floating layers (method picker, environment switcher, sheets) get a real shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.5) 0 8px 24px); notably the response/JSON code block sits on a DARKER surface than canvas, inverting the usual "elevated = lighter" rule to signal "this is machine output"

Distinctive named UI patterns (reproduce faithfully):
1. Method-colored URL/request bar — a single pill+field+send unit where a colored method segment (GET/POST/etc.) sits left of a monospace URL field, with a full-height orange Send button on the right
2. HTTP method color system — a fixed hue per method used identically in the URL bar, collection rows and history entries, so color is read before text
3. Status-code chip + timing readout — after a send: a colored pill status code, then elapsed time and response size, all set in monospace as "the developer's instant verdict"
4. Syntax-highlighted, collapsible JSON viewer — keys/strings/numbers/punctuation each get a distinct hue, never bold, with expandable tree nodes
5. Request-editor tab strip — a horizontal row of Params/Headers/Body/Auth/Pre-request/Tests tabs with a sliding underline in brand orange and a dot badge when a tab holds content
6. Environment pill with `{{variable}}` interpolation shown in orange wherever a template variable appears in a URL or body field
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Ration the brand orange strictly to actionable elements (Send, active tab underline, primary buttons, links) — it must never appear as a decorative fill or a second brand color.
2. Assign every HTTP method a fixed hue and reuse that exact hue everywhere the method appears (URL bar, collection rows, history) — never let a method's color drift between screens or soften only sometimes.
3. Set every piece of machine-originated data — URLs, header names/values, query params, JSON, status codes, timing figures — in the monospace face; set everything a human authored (labels, headings, prose) in the sans face. Never mix the two.
4. Color JSON syntax by role (key/string/number/punctuation) using hue alone, never using bold weight to carry syntax meaning.
5. Keep the response/JSON body's surface darker than the general canvas, deliberately inverting normal elevation logic, so "data" reads as sunk/output and "controls" read as floated/interactive.
6. Use the neutral dark grey canvas value specified above exactly — do not substitute a pure black or a blue-tinted charcoal, since Postman's console feel depends on true neutral grey.
7. Soften method and status hues for dark mode relative to their saturated light-mode values, but never change which hue represents which method or status class.
8. Keep the tiny uppercase eyebrow convention (e.g. section labels) restricted to genuinely small labels — never uppercase body prose or any machine data string.
9. Reserve real drop shadows for floating overlay layers only (pickers, sheets, dropdowns) — bordered surfaces at rest (URL bar, cards, inputs) should separate via a 1pt border and a lighter fill, not a shadow.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [name of the app you are building]
- Platform target: [iOS version, SwiftUI minimum deployment target]
- Protocol/request types supported: [REST/HTTP, GraphQL, WebSocket, gRPC, other]
- Method or operation-type taxonomy you need color-coded: [list your equivalent of GET/POST/PUT/etc.]
- Response format(s) to render: [JSON, XML, plain text, binary preview]

Working code for the post reader layout, the Subscribe/paywall card, the pull-quote treatment and a chronological inbox row

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in cloning editorial and publishing-platform interfaces into precise, production-ready SwiftUI. You understand the print-magazine design lineage behind long-form reading apps and why a subscription business rations its one brand color to a single conversion moment.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from a real newsletter/publishing platform's design system:

Color roles (light "Reader" theme default, dark theme supported):
- Paper white #FFFFFF (light reading page) / soft charcoal #121212 (dark reading page — never pure black)
- Reading ink #1F1F1F (warm near-black body text, not pure black), title ink #1A1A1A, subhead/dek ink #57534E, meta grey #8A8A8A, hairline #ECECEC
- App surfaces: subtle #F7F6F4 (light) / #1B1B1B-#262626 (dark), divider #E7E5E1 (light) / #2E2E2E (dark)
- The single brand + conversion accent is orange #FF6719, held IDENTICAL in light and dark, pressed #E5560E, with a soft tint wash #FFF7F2 (light) / #2A1C12 (dark) and tint border #FFD9C2 / #5C3A24 used only for the Subscribe/paywall card
- One secondary accent: link blue #4A6FE3, used only for inline hyperlinks inside body prose
- Semantic: error red #D93025, success green #1A8917

Type ladder (serif for anything read, Source Serif 4 or Spectral, fallback Georgia/Times New Roman; sans for anything operated, Inter, fallback -apple-system/SF Pro Text):
- Screen Title (serif) 30pt/700, Post Title (serif) 26pt/700, Section Heading in-post (serif) 22pt/700, Pull Quote (serif italic) 21pt/600, Reading Body (serif) 18pt/400 at 1.65 line-height, Subtitle/Dek (serif italic) 17pt/400, Button (sans) 15pt/700, Publication Label (sans) 14pt/600, Metadata (sans) 13pt/400, Publication Eyebrow (sans, uppercase) 11pt/700 +0.4pt tracking, Tab Label (sans) 10pt/600

Spacing / radius / shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/48; reading content inset 24pt horizontal (the editorial measure); app/chrome inset 16pt; paragraph spacing 18pt between body paragraphs
- Radius scale: 4pt inline chips/tags, 6pt the Subscribe button and search field, 8-10pt the Subscribe/paywall card and tier cards, 16pt sheets/modals, 500pt filter chips, 50% avatars and the unread dot
- The reading column itself is entirely flat — zero shadow, zero border, zero card background around prose; the Subscribe card stands out purely by its warm-orange tint and thin tint border, never by elevation; only transient floating elements (a sticky bottom bar, bottom sheets) get a faint shadow

Distinctive named UI patterns (reproduce faithfully):
1. Post reader — publication row (logo tile + name + subscriber count), serif title, italic serif dek, byline with avatar and read-time, long-form serif body at 18pt/1.65, with zero surrounding chrome
2. Sticky Subscribe / paywall-break card — a centered, orange-tinted card (never elevated by shadow) that interrupts a free preview with a price line and a full-width orange Subscribe button
3. Pull-quote — italic serif text with a signature 3pt orange left border rule and no background box, the single most recognizable in-body element
4. Inbox row (the home tab) — a square publication thumbnail, an uppercase orange publication-name eyebrow, a serif post title, sans byline metadata, and an orange unread dot; the whole tab is explicitly chronological, never algorithmic
5. Post action bar — Like (heart that fills orange with a pop animation), Comment, Restack, Share, all set in the sans operating typeface
6. The orange accent held pixel-identical between light and dark themes, functioning as the one constant conversion/attention signal across the whole app
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Set everything the reader consumes — titles, deks, body copy, pull-quotes, in-post section headings — in the reading serif; set everything the reader operates — buttons, tabs, labels, metadata — in the sans face. Never cross the two.
2. Ration the brand orange to the Subscribe CTA, the active tab, the unread indicator, the liked-heart fill and the pull-quote rule — nowhere else. A second accent color, or orange used decoratively, breaks the conversion signal.
3. Never wrap the reading column in a card, border or shadow — prose must appear to sit directly on bare paper, exactly like a printed page.
4. Keep the reading body's line-height generously loose (roughly 1.65) with a comfortable editorial measure — this is built for sustained long-form reading, not for skimming density.
5. Render the subtitle/dek in italic serif — this single typographic choice is what signals "magazine" rather than "app."
6. Distinguish the Subscribe/paywall card from the rest of the page by warm-orange color and a thin tint border only, never by adding elevation or shadow to it.
7. Make the home/inbox surface strictly chronological — never introduce an algorithmic ranking or a recommendation shuffle to what is meant to read as an email-replacement reading queue.
8. Hold the orange accent's exact hex value identical across light and dark themes; every other color may shift for the theme, but this one must not.
9. Keep comments and any short-form conversational surface in the sans operating face, never the reading serif — serif is reserved for the article itself, not for chrome-adjacent conversation.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [name of the app you are building]
- Platform target: [iOS version, SwiftUI minimum deployment target]
- Content type being published: [long-form articles, podcasts, video, mixed]
- Monetization model: [free, paid subscription, tiered, one-time]
- Home surface model: [chronological inbox/queue vs. a feed — describe]
- Existing brand accent color (if any) to reconcile against the single-orange rule: [hex or "none yet"]
- Companion short-form surface needed: [yes/no — a Notes-like feed]
- Screens in scope for this pass: [e.g. post reader, subscribe/paywall card, inbox, publication page]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` token extension matching the reading-serif/operating-sans split and the reference palette above, including light and dark variants with the accent held constant.
2. Working SwiftUI view code for the post reader layout (publication row, title, dek, byline, flowing body with inline pull-quote support).
3. The sticky Subscribe / paywall-break card component, including its tint background, price line, and full-width CTA.
4. A chronological inbox row component with the eyebrow label, 2-line title clamp, metadata line and unread dot.
5. The post action bar (like/comment/restack/share) with the heart-fill pop animation and haptic.
6. An accessibility pass covering VoiceOver labeling for the action bar and inbox rows, Dynamic Type behavior on serif reading text (including the user-adjustable reading-size setting), and contrast validation for ink-on-paper and orange-on-tint combinations.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Vercel Design System
summary: Recreate Vercel's pure-black, hairline-bordered developer console UI in SwiftUI, built around the deployment status traffic-light and Geist mono data typography.
description: A production-ready prompt for rebuilding Vercel's OLED-true-black iOS design system in SwiftUI, covering the deployments list, the Ready/Building/Error status system, and the sans-for-humans/mono-for-machines typographic split.

whatYouGet: A SwiftUI color and type token set for a pure-black, no-brand-accent developer console with a strict sans/mono content split
Working code for the deployment card with its status dot, environment tag and git metadata, plus a gridline-free analytics chart
House rules that protect true-black-not-charcoal, border-not-shadow elevation, and the status traffic-light as the only systemic color
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in cloning developer-infrastructure dashboards into precise, production-ready SwiftUI. You understand why a deployment platform strips out brand-color decoration entirely and instead spends its only color budget on communicating build/deploy state.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from a real cloud-deployment platform's design system:

Color roles (dark default, light is a clean inversion):
- Pure black canvas #000000 (true OLED black, explicitly NOT a softened charcoal like #191919)
- Surface 1 #0A0A0A (cards/rows — the one elevation step above canvas), Surface 2 #111111 (inset panels/charts), Surface 3 #1A1A1A (pressed/tag fill); Divider #2E2E2E, stronger border #333333
- Text: primary #EDEDED, secondary #A1A1A1, tertiary #707070
- There is no brand-accent CTA color: the primary interactive fill is a high-contrast off-white #EDEDED (pressed #CFCFCF); a secondary blue #0070F3 (hover #3291FF) is used only for links, focused-input borders and analytics
- Status traffic-light (the systemic accent): Ready/success #0CCE6B, Building/queued #F5A623, Error/canceled #E5484D, each with a ~10-12% opacity dim surface variant for pill/badge fills
- Decorative-only highlight gradient: purple #7928CA to cyan #50E3C2 (occasionally pink #FF0080), used exclusively for avatar placeholders, never in the core product chrome

Type ladder (Geist Sans for humans, Geist Mono for machine-generated strings, fallback sans -apple-system/SF Pro Text, fallback mono SF Mono/Menlo/Consolas):
- Display 32pt/800 -0.6pt tracking, Title 26pt/700, Section 22pt/700, Subsection 18pt/600, Body 16pt/400, Label 15pt/500, Body Strong 14pt/600, Meta 14pt/400, URL/Hash (mono) 13pt/400, Log Line (mono) 12pt/400, Caption 12pt/500 +0.2pt uppercase eyebrow, Tab Label 10pt/500, Button 14pt/600

Spacing / radius / shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt, scale 4/8/10/12/14/16/20/24/28/32/40/48; card internal padding 14pt; section gap 24pt; screen horizontal inset 16-18pt
- Radius scale: 4pt tiny tags/inline chips, 6pt environment tags, 8pt buttons/inputs/search field, 12pt deployment cards and panels, 16pt sheets/modals, 999pt pill status badges, 50% avatars and status dots
- There is essentially one elevation step and shadows are nearly absent: bordered surfaces (cards, panels, inputs) use only a 1pt hairline border with no shadow at all; only genuinely floating overlays (sheets, popovers) get a real shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.6) 0 8px 24px) plus a slightly stronger border

Distinctive named UI patterns (reproduce faithfully):
1. Deployment card — a status dot (with a soft halo of the same color) + state label + environment tag on row one, the deployment URL in monospace on row two, and git branch + relative time on row three; this list is the entire home screen
2. Status dot + state — a 9pt colored dot whose halo pulses while "Building", then cross-fades from amber to green on completion with a success haptic
3. Environment tag — a small monospace pill reading "Production"/"Preview"/"Development", low-chroma fill, display-only (not tappable)
4. Gridline-free analytics chart — bar/line charts rendered in the secondary blue on a slightly-elevated panel with zero gridlines and zero axis ornament, sparse mono axis labels only
5. Triangle logomark — a single-fill equilateral triangle that is never gradient-filled, outlined, or rotated
6. Build-log viewer — full-bleed pure-black background, monospace log lines with ANSI-mapped colors, auto-scrolling to the tail with a "jump to bottom" affordance when the user scrolls away
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The dark canvas must be literal, pure #000000 — never a softened charcoal — because true-black-behind-hairline-borders is the single most identifying trait of this system.
2. There is no brand-accent CTA: the primary button is always a high-contrast white/off-white fill, never a tinted brand color — resist the urge to add one even for a new feature's "hero" action.
3. Set every machine-produced string — URLs, branch names, commit hashes, environment variable values, log lines, durations — in the monospace face; set everything a human wrote in the sans face. This split must be treated as non-negotiable.
4. Reserve the status traffic-light (green/amber/red) exclusively for build/deploy state — never repurpose those three hues for unrelated UI meaning like generic success/warning/error toasts elsewhere.
5. Elevate surfaces with a single lighter step plus a 1pt hairline border, never a drop shadow, for anything at rest (cards, panels, inputs) — reserve real shadows only for layers that are genuinely floating above the page (sheets, popovers, dropdowns).
6. Keep the purple-to-cyan gradient confined to avatar placeholders only; it must never appear as a chrome background, button fill, or chart color in the core product.
7. Never add gridlines, axis ticks or chart ornament to analytics visualizations — sparseness itself is the intended signature, and whitespace should function as the implicit grid.
8. Keep tab-switch and other primary navigation transitions instant with no slide animation — this product favors immediacy over transitional motion everywhere except the status-dot color cross-fade.
9. Keep the triangle logomark (or your product's equivalent geometric mark) a single flat fill at all times — never gradient-fill it, outline it, or rotate it for emphasis.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product context: [name of the app you are building]
- Platform target: [iOS version, SwiftUI minimum deployment target]
- Core entity being monitored: [deployments / builds / jobs / pipelines — whatever populates the list]
- Status states you need to represent: [e.g. Ready, Building, Error, Canceled, Queued — map to your domain]
- Analytics or metrics surface needed: [yes/no, and which metrics]
- Existing brand accent color (if any) to reconcile against the "no CTA accent" rule: [hex or "none yet"]
- Log or console output surface needed: [yes/no]
- Screens in scope for this pass: [e.g. list/home, item detail, analytics, settings]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` token extension matching the reference palette (including the status traffic-light and dim-surface variants) and the sans/mono type ladder above.
2. Working SwiftUI view code for the deployment (or equivalent status) card, the environment tag, and the status-dot component with its Building-state pulse and Ready-state color cross-fade.
3. A gridline-free analytics chart component in the secondary blue, with sparse monospace axis labels only.
4. A full-bleed build-log/console viewer with ANSI-style color mapping and auto-scroll-to-tail behavior.
5. A motion/haptics cheat sheet for the status transition, pull-to-refresh, sheet presentation and button press states.
6. An accessibility pass covering VoiceOver labeling for status dots and tags (color is never the only signal), Dynamic Type behavior for mono vs. sans elements, and a note on why borders replace shadows on this palette.
</what_to_give_me>
